findings.description: The new configured-provider path admits `http://` endpoints to RFC1918 IP literals when `allow_insecure_endpoint` matches, and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <configured>` will probe `<endpoint>/models`. If a repository-controlled or otherwise untrusted `.loa.config.yaml` is loaded, this becomes an SSRF primitive against internal network services. The diff-touched trigger is `tests/unit/model-health-probe-configured-provider.bats`, which validates probing arbitrary configured providers through this policy. The policy prevents DNS rebinding, but it still allows direct private IP targets such as `10.0.0.5` or `192.168.1.1`.
findings.recommendation: Restrict health-probe configured providers to loopback by default, or require an explicit trusted-config source for RFC1918 targets. At minimum, separate `allow_insecure_endpoint` for local model dispatch from probe reachability and refuse private non-loopback probing unless an operator-controlled flag is set outside repo config.

findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/adversarial-review-locality.bats: @test "LOC-7 a local entry whose fallback_chain reaches a hosted model is hosted (cheval would walk it inside the call)" and @test "LOC-10 ..."
findings.cross_file_justification: LOC-10 (diff) proves the cheval loader admits localbox:qwen-leaky (dispatch_group: local with fallback_chain: ["openai:gpt-5.5"]). LOC-7 (diff) proves only the planner's stdlib mirror .claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py classifies it hosted. The P0 file .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py::validate_providers enforces the local-hop rule on the endpoint host only and never inspects fallback_chain.
findings.description: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices the stated guarantee is that every hosted hop is refused by name at plan time and never rerouted. The loader's local-hop rule in validate_providers checks the provider's endpoint host and CLI-ness, but a dispatch_group: local model whose own fallback_chain reaches a hosted model loads without complaint (LOC-10 lists qwen-leaky among the admitted models). The fallback_chain_reaches_hosted classification exists only in the planner mirror hop-locality.py. The module docstring names two further mirrors that implement the host rule alone (Bridgebuilder config.ts localEndpointHost and the request-time TransportPolicy, which is bound per model/provider, not per locality mode). Any consumer that classifies by host passes qwen-leaky as local, and cheval walks the hosted fallback inside the call using the hosted adapter's unconstrained transport (proxies honoured, redirects followed, public host allowed).
findings.failure_mode: An operator who chose local_voices to keep the diff and system prompt on-premises has them sent to a hosted provider through an in-call fallback, while the planner's inventory and MODELINV show the hop as planned local. The refuse-by-name promise is broken silently, and the config example in this diff documents the opposite behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce in validate_providers (the 'ONE implementation' the docstring claims): refuse at load any dispatch_group: local model whose fallback_chain, resolved through aliases, reaches a hop that fails the local-hop rule, with the same reason text hop-locality.py emits. Independently, make cheval's fallback walker refuse crossing from a local hop to a non-local one when the dispatch carries locality_mode: local_voices, so the guarantee no longer depends on every planner mirror agreeing.

findings.trigger_anchor: .loa.config.yaml.example @@ -2411,6 +2505,15 @@ (exit_on_degraded comment: 'read from the trusted config ... never from the PR head')
findings.description: secret_env_allowlist is the only control that stops a provider's auth: "{env:VAR}" from reading an arbitrary environment variable into a bearer token. The Azure and local examples added in this diff show the allowlist is extended from the same hounfour: block of the same .loa.config.yaml that declares the provider, its endpoint and its auth. A control that the governed file can widen is a typo guard, not a security boundary: whoever can edit the config can add ^GITHUB_TOKEN$ (or any CI secret) to the allowlist, point a provider at a public https endpoint (the validator admits any public https host), alias a voice to it, and the first request carries the secret. The exit_on_degraded comment in the same diff says that on a pull request *that key* is read from the trusted base-branch config and never from the PR head, which implies other keys, including providers, aliases, advisory_voices and the allowlist, may be read from the PR head by Bridgebuilder.
findings.failure_mode: A pull request edits .loa.config.yaml to add a provider at an attacker-controlled https endpoint with auth bound to a CI secret plus the matching allowlist pattern, and lists it as a voice or advisory voice. Bridgebuilder's first request exfiltrates the token. If Bridgebuilder already reads the whole hounfour block from the trusted config, the remaining risk is that the example documents a bypass of the allowlist for any other consumer that trusts a checked-out config.
findings.suggested_fix: On pull requests, read hounfour.providers, hounfour.aliases, hounfour.secret_env_allowlist and flatline_protocol.*.advisory_voices from the same trusted config path used for exit_on_degraded, and state that in the example next to secret_env_allowlist. Consider making the allowlist extensible only from the environment or the trusted config, not from the project file, and refuse an auth: "{env:...}" outside the built-in list when the config file is group- or world-writable or comes from a PR head.

findings.anchor: @test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse"
findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats BUD-3 and the _cfg fixture (hounfour.providers.*.models.*.pricing overlay)
findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/ledger.py::create_ledger_entry prices every real call from find_pricing on the same merged config; a {0,0} overlay yields cost_micro_usd 0 with pricing_source 'config', so the daily budget counter in update_daily_spend never advances either.
findings.description: The budget pre-check now prices each planned voice from the catalog as overlaid by the project config. BUD-3 asserts a zero-priced entry estimates 0 cents and passes even a 0-cent budget. The overlay is not restricted to local or keyless providers: a pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0} placed on openai.models.gpt-5.5 zeroes the pre-call estimate for a hosted model, and the ledger then records every real call at cost 0 as a 'config' price, so neither the per-run budget_cents nor metering.budget.daily_micro_usd ever trips.
findings.failure_mode: A mistaken or malicious overlay removes both cost controls for a hosted model at once; spend is unbounded and cost-report shows 0 for the affected hops.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a zero catalog price as 'no catalog price' (fixed 10/30 fallback) unless the hop is local (dispatch_group local on a loopback or RFC1918 endpoint) or the provider is keyless; or require an explicit zero_priced: true acknowledgement on the model entry. In create_ledger_entry, mark a hosted row priced at 0 from an overlay with a distinct pricing_source so cost-report can flag it.

findings.trigger_anchor: .loa.config.yaml.example Example 4 comment: 'an IP literal or localhost ... that is never resolved through DNS ... the name cannot be rebound'
findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py::local_host and local_endpoint_host accept the literal 'localhost' through the validator's check_insecure_optin; TransportPolicy is described as comparing the request host string, not the connected peer address.
findings.description: The new Example 4 comment claims the insecure-endpoint host is never resolved through DNS and cannot be rebound. That is true for IP literals but not for 'localhost', which the local-hop rule accepts. 'localhost' is a name resolved by the system resolver; its mapping depends on /etc/hosts and nsswitch order, and some resolvers forward it to DNS. The request-time check compares the host string, so a non-loopback resolution is not detected.
findings.failure_mode: On a host where localhost resolves off-loopback (missing /etc/hosts entry, hostile resolver), an http:// local provider sends prompts in clear text to that address while every layer reports hop_locality local and the operator believes the documented guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Under local_voices and for http opt-ins, require an IP literal and refuse 'localhost', or resolve it via getaddrinfo at connect time and refuse any non-loopback result; correct the example comment to say IP literals are not resolved and localhost is checked at connect time.

findings.anchor: @test "LOC-4 one local family on the audit gate: the companion is duplicate_voice, the DEGRADED sentence is in the output, and the gate and verdict-derive treat the envelope as today"
findings.trigger_anchor: .loa.config.yaml.example @@ -813,6 +813,24 @@ (locality comment: 'every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other')
findings.description: Under locality: local_voices with one local family, every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW by design, and LOC-4 asserts the COMPLETED gate opens and verdict-derive reports consistent/APPROVED exactly as for a two-family audit. The degradation exists only as a stderr sentence, a metadata.locality.note string and free text in the feedback file. No machine-read field in verdict_quality changes and no operator acknowledgement is required, so a single local model (often a small open-weight one) silently becomes the entire security review.
findings.failure_mode: A sprint ships with a security verdict that is indistinguishable in every machine-read field from a full two-family audit; downstream gates, dashboards and the COMPLETED hook cannot tell them apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Write a machine-readable verdict_quality.degraded_reason (e.g. locality_single_family) and carry a degraded flag in the LOA-VERDICT comment that verdict-derive parses; require an explicit flatline_protocol.security_audit.allow_degraded_locality: true before the COMPLETED gate opens for such an envelope.
